$comment: Cross-client parity matrix. Both runners read this file verbatim and configure through the same ordered calls, so neither can drift from the other. Base parameters are buckley_case_a from src/lib/ressim/src/tests/buckley.rs. `strict` cases must agree to 1e-9; non-strict ones still diverge across targets and report the gap instead of failing -- see the FIM note in docs/ARCHITECTURE_SPLIT_PLAN_2026-09-19.md.

cases.why: The original fixture. Three steps leaves the front mid-grid; a fully swept or static field would agree without proving much.

The same case on the implicit solver. Strict since the linear routing was unified on 2026-09-22: it was 8.282e+00 bar apart across targets and is now 5.7e-14. Keeping it strict is what stops the cfg(target_arch) split coming back.
Mobility ratio is the axis the catalog's sensitivities vary most. A favourable displacement moves the front differently and exercises the relperm path at different saturations.

Adverse mobility on the implicit solver, the case most likely to need timestep cuts. NOT strict: unifying the linear routing took it from 1.733e+00 bar to 1.24e-05, so the dominant cause is gone but a second, smaller one remains -- see OPEN_ITEMS section 1. Reported every run so the residual stays measured.

A different cell count changes array sizes across the boundary, and grid refinement is a numerics sensitivity in its own right. Short step because 12 highly permeable cells sweep in well under a day, and parity measured on a uniform field proves nothing (front lands at 5 of 12).
